clue.text: Wander around to escape pesky insect

parts.note: to gad or gad about is to wander around idly
to fly is to flee or escape

explanation.surface: Someone advises roaming about to get away from an annoying bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a horsefly or botfly that bites livestock, the archetypal irritating bug.

clue.text: Switch positions intermittently

explanation.surface: A switch can be in two settings, used now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A light switch has two settings, live and dead; the phrase also means sporadically, now and again.

clue.text: One strips off, after rising in a dream?

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: peels means strips off, as of a skin

explanation.surface: Someone undresses after getting up, half awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' is the reversal signal in a down clue; 'in a dream?' looks like part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is in a dream state; the question mark marks the loose equivalence.

clue.text: Boy snatching female underwear or dog

indicators.note: the boy grabs the garment and holds it inside himself, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a bra is a woman's undergarment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lad grabs a woman's lingerie, or perhaps it was the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of retriever dog.

clue.text: Finds Fiat car crashed round large road obstacle

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the one for large
a crashed car is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a Fiat smashed into a big roadside barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns FINDSFIATCAR into TRAFFICISAND; 'round' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised island in the road channels traffic and is a solid thing drivers must steer around.

clue.text: Film one patiently suffering in Rome

parts.note: someone from Rome is an Italian, so the figure in Rome is described as the Italian
Job of the Old Testament is the byword for patience under suffering

explanation.surface: A movie about a long-suffering person living in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1969 caper film starring Michael Caine is read as the biblical Job, transplanted to Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1969 British heist movie about stealing gold in Turin.

clue.text: Trim feathers to inhibit brash display

definitions.text: Trim feathers to inhibit brash display

parts.words: Trim feathers to inhibit brash display
parts.note: the picture is clipping a showy bird's plumage so it cannot strut, read as humbling a boastful person

explanation.surface: Clip a peacock's plumage so it can no longer show off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means humbling someone conceited, reducing their swagger.

clue.text: New view of fine face, in old frame, offering nothing stimulating?

indicators.note: the old word surrounds the reworked letters like a picture frame

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned

indicators.note: a new view rearranges the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fresh portrait of a handsome face set in an antique frame, yet dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New view of' signals the anagram and 'frame' the container; the question mark flags that decaf coffee is a jokey example of something dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with its caffeine removed provides no stimulant.

clue.text: Complaint about Labour PM reducing farmer's stock

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: reducing cuts the name short, taking off its final letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was Labour Prime Minister of the UK from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A grievance about a Labour leader cutting farm subsidies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reducing' drops the last E of ATTLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows raised for meat form part of a farmer's livestock.

clue.text: King and in German? That's priceless!

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
the German first-person pronoun is ich

explanation.surface: A Rodgers and Hammerstein musical retitled for Germany, greeted as hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the musical The King and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich used as an exclamation means outrageously funny or absurd, like the cry 'priceless!'.

clue.text: Stop roaming, avoiding river

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving something out, here the letter for river

parts.note: stray means wandering or roaming
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Quit wandering and keep away from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain, halting further movement.

clue.text: Went out, being left

explanation.surface: Someone faded away after being abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping off is falling asleep, going out like a light; something set down and left somewhere has been delivered.

clue.text: A measure of how difficult it is to understand geometry?

definitions.text: A measure of how difficult it is to understand geometry?

parts.words: A measure of how difficult it is to understand geometry?
parts.note: the graph of progress in acquiring a skill is reread as studying a line from geometry

explanation.surface: A gauge of how hard geometry is to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: The graph plotting skill against experience measures how hard something is to master.

clue.text: Attractive? Entirely, and 19 -use the phone

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely
the answer to 19 across is abbreviated to the letter U
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: An instruction to call everyone at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluring means enticing or charming.

clue.text: Meet to study roadside

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a verge is the grass strip at the edge of a road

explanation.surface: Gather to look at the edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that converge come together at one point.

clue.text: Apostle nob's represented here?

indicators.note: represented means shown again in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter, leaving nob

explanation.surface: A head of a disciple is depicted on this.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostle spoon has a figure of an apostle on the handle, so its knob, the nob, is an apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: Large serving spoons were made as apostle spoons, whose handle tops bear a saint's figure.

clue.text: Elevated positions getting men in fuddled state

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means raised upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: puts means places or positions
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: High rank comes with soldiers who are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, befuddled condition.

clue.text: Religious figure, male, taking on Knight

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess notation for king, but knight as an honour is abbreviated K, as in KBE

explanation.surface: A man of faith takes on a knight in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar or brother living under vows in a monastery is a religious figure.

clue.text: Accident is hard to locate in chart

indicators.note: to locate one thing in another is to place it inside

parts.note: a map is a chart
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An accident is difficult to find on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is a minor accident or misfortune.

clue.text: Not locked? That's a shock

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: Finding the door unlocked comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A door slightly open is unfastened, so certainly unlocked.

clue.text: United retreating in truth infiltrated by first of strikers from Academicals?

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in football club names

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for truth is entered by a letter from within

parts.note: verity means truth

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of strikers

explanation.surface: A football report: United falling back as a forward from Academicals breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' signals the reversal and 'infiltrated by' the container. Academicals is a Scottish football club name (Hamilton Academical), and also means students and dons.
explanation.definitionFit: Academics and students make up a university, the home of academicals.

clue.text: National icon, as the white cliffs of Dover appear from the Channel?

definitions.text: National icon, as the white cliffs of Dover appear from the Channel?

parts.words: National icon, as the white cliffs of Dover appear from the Channel?
parts.note: the UK central bank is an institution; the chalk cliffs seen from sea are a shore, an edge of the country

explanation.surface: Dover's chalk cliffs seen from a ship, a symbol of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The white cliffs of Dover are a famous chalk coastline in Kent facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's central bank is a national institution; the cliffs are literally the coast or shore of the country.
